correctness.rationale: For K positive definite and one hostile bridge, the signed FJ energy is strictly convex. The within-community Dirichlet minimum is A(u-1)^2/2 with A=1/(K_U+L_U)^{-1}_{aa} and similarly B, giving the claimed exact closed form after solving a 2x2 positive-definite problem. Strict positivity and bounds 0<h,g<=1 follow from the inverse-positive M-matrix and maximum principle. The threshold coefficients 2Bh_i-(A+B) and 2Ag_j-(A+B) cannot simultaneously be positive on opposite sides. Their strict superlevel sets are rooted and connected by the killed-harmonic averaging equation. The independent full-system standard-library rational checker passed 4556 cases including exact threshold equalities; these finite checks are corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: For a standard signed-network opinion model with fully unanimous positive personal views, the theorem resolves a motivated structural question: whether one hostile intercommunity link can produce expressed dissent. It supplies a sharp if-and-only-if effective-anchoring criterion, exact individual hostility thresholds, rooted connectedness and nestedness of the flipping region on arbitrary finite positive networks. A three-node uniform-stubbornness example shows topology alone can reverse an opinion; a second example produces two distinct spatial reversal thresholds. This supplies interpretable topology-dependent predictions beyond computing one equilibrium or extending a textbook formula.
